context.problem_statement: Fit a Gaussian model to spectroscopy data to characterize a spectral peak. The Gaussian function is: f(x) = amplitude * exp(-((x - mu) / (2*sigma))^2) + baseline. Use scipy.optimize.curve_fit to estimate: amplitude (peak height), mu (peak center wavelength in nm), sigma (peak width), and baseline (background signal). Report the fitted parameters with 95% confidence intervals (from the covariance matrix). Also compute the Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM = 2.355 * sigma) and the peak area (amplitude * sigma * sqrt(2*pi)).
context.expert_knowledge: Gaussian: f(x) = A * exp(-0.5*((x-mu)/sigma)^2) + B. Initial parameter guesses: A = max(signal) - min(signal), mu = x at max(signal), sigma = estimated from peak width, B = min(signal). FWHM = 2*sqrt(2*ln(2))*sigma ≈ 2.355*sigma. Peak area = integral of Gaussian = A*sigma*sqrt(2*pi). Confidence interval: estimate ± 1.96*sqrt(pcov diagonal). Check convergence: residual sum of squares should be small.
